[=Surface Language=]

[==Shape==]

In this repository, SPO is an expression-oriented language with:

- pattern matching as a core mechanism
- algebraic data forms built from [.txt|().], [.txt|Pair.], [.txt|Prefix.], and [.txt|Record.]
- an explicit type language with recursion and generics
- file-based modules via [.txt|§IMPORT.] and [.txt|§EXPORT.]
- a small imperative corner through [.txt|§VAR.] and methods

Many visible forms are sugar. Internally, the implementation reduces a lot of syntax to pairs, prefixes, records, normal calls, and [.txt|§IF ... MATCH.].

[.mermaid
|flowchart TD
|	MOD["Module"] --> IMP["§IMPORT Pattern"]
|	MOD --> CMD["Commands"]
|	MOD --> EXP["§EXPORT Expression"]
|
|	CMD --> DEF["§DEF"]
|	CMD --> VAR["§VAR / Method Calls"]
|	CMD --> REC["§RECURSIVE"]
|	CMD --> RET["§RETURN"]
|
|	EXP --> LIT["Literals"]
|	EXP --> DATA["Tuple / Pair / Prefix / Record"]
|	EXP --> CALL["Calls / Pipes"]
|	EXP --> CTRL["§IF / MATCH / §IS"]
|	EXP --> FUNC["Lambda / Method / Block"]
|	EXP --> TYPE["Type Literals"]
.]

[==Lexical Form==]

From [.txt|mTokenizer.]:

- keywords are [.txt|§.]-prefixed special ids such as [.txt|§DEF.], [.txt|§IF.], [.txt|§IMPORT.]
- prefix constructors use [.txt|#.]
- normal identifiers may contain [.txt|....]
- char literals are currently forms like [.txt|§a.], [.txt|§A.], [.txt|§1.], and are therefore limited to alphanumeric single characters
- strings can be single-line or multi-line

Multi-line text has this form:

[.spo
|"
||first line
||second line
|"
.]

[==Module Form==]

A SPO module consists of:

o 1. optional [.txt|§IMPORT.]
o 2. zero or more commands
o 3. mandatory [.txt|§EXPORT.]

If [.txt|§IMPORT.] is absent, the parser inserts an empty record pattern internally.

Example:

[.spo
|§IMPORT {
|	Std: {
|		...+...: §DEF ...+... € [[§INT, §INT] => §INT]
|	}
|}
|
|§DEF Inc = (
|	§DEF X € §INT
|) => X .+ 1
|
|§EXPORT Inc
.]

Important: [.txt|§IMPORT.] is a pattern, not just a name list. Modules are matched as structured values.

[==Internal Names at the IL Boundary==]

The SPO surface does not show all internal names directly. In generated [.txt|.ILT.] and in VM traces, these additional forms appear:

- module imports such as [.txt|Std:.] or [.txt|Char:.] become internal field names [.txt|_Std.] and [.txt|_Char.]
- local and bound SPO names often appear underscore-prefixed, such as [.txt|_X.] or [.txt|_Char.]
- compiler-generated register, def, and type names are [.txt|r_*.], [.txt|d_*.], and [.txt|t_*.]

This is not a second user-facing language layer, but it is a real architectural boundary when comparing [.txt|.SPO.], [.txt|.ILT.], and runtime traces.

[==Commands==]

The command forms implemented by the parser are:

- [.txt|Pattern = Expression.]
- [.txt|§RETURN Expression.]
- [.txt|§RETURN Expression IF Expression.]
- [.txt|§VAR Name := Expression ... ..]
- [.txt|Expression : MethodCalls ..]
- [.txt|§RECURSIVE { ... }.]

Examples from real tests:

[.spo
|{Second: §DEF x} = {First: (), Second: 1}
|
|§VAR X := 1, + 2 .
|
|§RECURSIVE {
|	§DEF Fib = (
|		§DEF n € §INT
|	) => ...
|}
.]

[===Blocks===]

Blocks are expressions:

[.spo
|{
|	§RETURN 1 IF cond
|	§RETURN 0
|}
.]

There is no implicit "last expression wins". Returns happen through explicit [.txt|§RETURN.] commands.

[==Expressions==]

[===Literals===]

- [.txt|().]
- [.txt|§TRUE.], [.txt|§FALSE.]
- integers such as [.txt|12.], [.txt|-3.], [.txt|1_000.]
- chars such as [.txt|§a.]
- text such as [.txt|"abc".]

[===Data Forms===]

[.spo
|#Box 12
|(a; b)
|(a, b, c)
|{ Name: "Ada", Age: 42 }
.]

Semantically important:

- tuples are sugar over nested pairs
- records are internally built from prefixed fields
- text values become recursive char lists

[===Calls and Operator-Style Names===]

SPO uses [.txt|....] inside names to create different call styles.

Examples from the repository:

- [.txt|2 .+ 5.] calls [.txt|...+....]
- [.txt|k .* a.] calls [.txt|...*....]
- [.txt|a .Ord.] calls [.txt|...Ord.]
- [.txt|3 .<= 5 <= 7.] chains [.txt|...<=...<=....]

The parser helpers [.txt|Infix.], [.txt|InfixCall.], and [.txt|InfixPrefix.] in [.txt|mSPO_Parser.] generate these names systematically.

[===Lambdas===]

Normal lambda:

[.spo
|(§DEF X € §INT) => X
.]

Generic lambda:

[.spo
|(§DEF t € §TYPE) <=> (
|	§DEF X € t
|) => X
.]

[===Methods===]

Methods have an object side and an argument side:

[.spo
|§DEF +... = (
|	§VAR X € §INT
|) : (
|	§DEF Y € §INT
|) {
|	X := ((§TO_VAL X) .+ Y).
|}
.]

Method calls can appear as statement-like chains and end with [.txt|..].

[===Pipes===]

Both directions are implemented:

[.spo
|Value §>.MapEachWith Mapper
|.Push 3 To §< .Push 2 To §< ()
.]

[.txt|mSPO_Desugar.] rewrites pipes into normal calls.

[===Control and Matching===]

If with conditions:

[.spo
|§IF {
|	Cond1: Expr1
|	Cond2: Expr2
|}
.]

Pattern match:

[.spo
|§IF Value MATCH {
|	Pattern1: Expr1
|	Pattern2: Expr2
|}
.]

[.txt|§IS.] is only sugar:

[.spo
|Pair §IS (_, 2)
|TagValue §IS (#Foo 12)
.]

Internally, [.txt|§IS.] is desugared to [.txt|§IF ... MATCH.].

[==Patterns==]

Pattern forms supported by parser and AST:

- [.txt|_.]
- identifier binding
- [.txt|§DEF Name.]
- [.txt|§VAR Name.]
- tuple and pair patterns
- record patterns
- prefix patterns such as [.txt|#Foo _.]
- typed patterns [.txt|Pattern € TypeExpr.]
- guard patterns [.txt|Pattern & Expr.]
- literal patterns

Examples from [.txt|Regression.Tests.]:

[.spo
|{Second: §DEF x} = {First: (), Second: 1}
|
|§IF (#Box 7) MATCH {
|	(#Box _): 1
|	_: 0
|}
.]

[==Type Language==]

[===Atomic Types===]

- [.txt|[[]].]
- [.txt|§BOOL.]
- [.txt|§INT.]
- [.txt|§CHAR.]
- [.txt|§TEXT.]
- [.txt|§ANY.]
- [.txt|§TYPE.]

[===Composite Types===]

- [.txt|[[A, B, C]].]
- [.txt|[[A; B]].]
- [.txt|[[A [|] B [|] C]].]
- [.txt|[[#Tag T]].]
- [.txt|[[§VAR T]].]
- [.txt|[[Arg => Res]].]
- [.txt|[[Obj : Arg => Res]].]

[===Abstract Type Forms===]

- [.txt|[[§RECURSIVE t Body]].]
- [.txt|[[§GENERIC t Body]].]
- [.txt|[[§INTERFACE t Body]].]
- [.txt|[[.tArray t]].] for generic type application

Architecturally important:

- this is the SPO surface syntax
- the IL text form uses different keywords for the same concepts:
  [.txt|§REC.], [.txt|§ALL.], and [.txt|§ANY.]
- when reading SPO and [.txt|.ILT.] side by side, that notation difference should not be confused with a semantic contradiction

[==SPO Syntax vs IL Text==]

[| [*Concept*] | [*SPO*] | [*IL*] |]
[| recursive type | [.txt||[[§RECURSIVE t T]].] | [.txt||[[§REC t => T]].] |]
[| generic type | [.txt||[[§GENERIC t T]].] | [.txt||[[§ALL t => T]].] |]
[| interface type | [.txt||[[§INTERFACE t T]].] | [.txt||[[§ANY t => T]].] |]
[| function call in IL | surface syntax like [.txt||a .F b.] | [.txt||r := .f a.] |]
[| method call in IL | surface syntax like [.txt||Obj : F Arg ..] | [.txt||r := §OBJ:f a.] |]

Examples from real regressions:

[.spo
|§DEF tIntArray = [§RECURSIVE tIntArray [[] | [tIntArray; §INT]]]
|
|§DEF tStack... = [§GENERIC t [§RECURSIVE tStack [[] | [t, tStack]]]]
|
|§DEF tArray... = [§GENERIC t [§RECURSIVE tArray [[] | [tArray; t]]]]
.]

[==Internal Models Behind the Sugar==]

[.mermaid
|flowchart LR
|	TUP["(a, b, c)"] --> PAIR["(((); a); b); c"]
|	TEXT["\"abc\""] --> CHARS["(#_Char... 97, #_Char... 98, #_Char... 99)"]
|	IS["expr §IS pattern"] --> MATCH["§IF expr MATCH { pattern: §TRUE; _: §FALSE }"]
|	PIPE["pipe syntax"] --> CALL["normal call chains"]
|	MOD["§IMPORT/§EXPORT"] --> INIT["ImportPattern => { ...; RETURN Export }"]
.]

Especially important:

- [.txt|§CHAR.] is internally a prefix over [.txt|§INT.]
- [.txt|§TEXT.] is internally a recursive type of [.txt|[[]].] or [.txt|[[Text; Char]].]
- tuples and text values are heavily reduced before final lowering

[==Language Limits That Should Not Be Hidden==]

- [.txt|§INTERFACE.] is visible in parser, AST, and type analysis, but not broadly secured end-to-end
- conditional types are not yet a finished feature
- generic type application works in regressions, but is not yet stable enough for the [.txt|Maybe.] module
- not every type-literal form is already fully implemented as a runtime value
